stem: Which characteristic is a hallmark of a normal neonatal ECG compared to an adult ECG?

options.text: A predominance of the right ventricle.
A predominance of the left ventricle.
A completely flat line between the P-wave and QRS complex.

explanation: Because the right ventricle is dominant during fetal life, neonates typically show right axis deviation and prominent R waves in anterior leads.
rationale: Think about which side of the heart works harder before birth.

optionExplanations.A: Because the right ventricle is dominant during fetal life, neonates typically show right axis deviation and prominent R waves in anterior leads.
optionExplanations.B: Left ventricular dominance is the typical pattern for teenagers and adults, but not for neonates.
optionExplanations.C: Neonates and babies actually have much faster heart rates compared to adults.
optionExplanations.D: While this is a normal feature, it is common to both healthy adults and children and does not distinguish a neonatal ECG.

source.hint: Think about which side of the heart works harder before birth.
